opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Ellison (employee ID E040) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E040.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Ellison (E040) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Payroll Specialist does not own it, so admin is not permitted. Full-time employees max out at write here. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jacob Ellison (E040) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; admin is never allowed. Since training is basic, max is read. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read. Note: Security DB employment type (contractor) differs from HR note (full_time).
reason: Jacob Ellison (E040) requests admin to Source Code. Per HR (authoritative for employment status), he is full-time and a Payroll Specialist. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Payroll Specialist does not own it, so admin is not permitted; full-time employees max out at write. Because the requested admin exceeds the maximum of write, grant write. (Note: Security's note claims contractor status and recommends read, but employment type per HR is full_time.)
